name: Plausible

pricing.notes: Official pages checked 2026-07-30; Starter listed at $9/month and Business at $19/month in public plan references.
pricing.freeTier: No free plan, just a 30-day trial; the open source version is free to self-host.

verdictSummary: Basic pageview/event analytics are easy, and Plausible's own code is open source; the paid value is hosted reliability, maintenance, and support.
coreLoopDIY: Add a small JS tracker, collect pageviews/events, aggregate by path/referrer/country/device, and show a dashboard.
whatYouLose: fast queries at millions of pageviews
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because analytics must be boring, fast, and legally safer without ops.

priorArt.name: plausible/analytics
priorArt.desc: Plausible itself is open source; self-host it

alternatives.name: GoatCounter
alternatives.desc: Even simpler than Plausible, which is either refreshing or a warning.

alternatives.name: Plausible Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Plausible without the hosted bill; you keep the core dashboard and inherit the Compose stack.

alternatives.name: Rybbit
alternatives.desc: Plausible's core plus replay and funnels, in exchange for a busier dashboard.

alternatives.name: Umami
alternatives.desc: The closest broad substitute: simple traffic analytics, events and goals with your data attached.

alternatives.name: Drift
alternatives.desc: Free and simple analytics for builders.

notes: Script + ingest + dashboard is a weekend. The data pipeline polish; bot filtering, sessionization at scale; is the real product. Both are open source: self-hosting is the honest move here.
prompt:
Build me a privacy-first web analytics tool like Plausible (personal scale).
Requirements:

- A <2KB tracking snippet (vanilla JS, no cookies): sends pageview beacons with
  path, referrer, screen class, and a daily-rotating visitor hash computed
  server-side from IP + user-agent + a salt (never store raw IPs).
- An ingest endpoint that filters obvious bots by user-agent and writes to
  SQLite. One row per event; index on (site, date).
- A /dashboard (basic-auth from .env): unique visitors, pageviews, top pages,
  top referrers, and countries for today/7d/30d, with a visitors-per-day bar
  chart as inline SVG. Fast and clean, dark mode.
- Sessionization: a visit ends after 30 idle minutes; compute bounce rate.
- Multi-site support via a site id in the snippet.
- Node or Python, one process. Honest note in the README: at serious traffic,
  self-host the real Plausible instead · this is for personal sites.
